aboutH2: HOPE Be The Cure: Residential Addiction Treatment in Innisfil, Ontario
intro: HOPE Be The Cure is a small private rehab in Innisfil, just south of Barrie. Adults with alcohol or drug addiction live at the house during treatment, and there are only five beds, so the group stays small and the staff know everyone by name. The centre gives its staffing ratio as 1 to 3.

The week is built around counselling. You get two one-to-one sessions a week with a certified addiction counsellor, group workshops every day and at least three 12-step meetings a week. Exercise, yoga, meditation, reiki, gardening and cooking classes take up much of the rest of the day.

pillars.title: A Five-Bed House in Innisfil
pillars.body: The program runs in a house on Pinegrove Avenue in Innisfil, a few minutes from the Lake Simcoe shore and a short drive from Barrie. Photos on the centre's profile show an open kitchen with a long dining table, a screened porch, a living room with big windows and simple bedrooms with two single beds. Clients can have a private or a shared room. With five beds there is no crowd, and meals are cooked from a menu that changes every week, partly with vegetables from the house garden.

pillars.title: A Weekly Group for Graduates and Their Families
pillars.body: When you finish the residential stay, you can keep coming back to a 90-minute aftercare group held in person once a week. A certified addictions counsellor leads it, and the topics are practical: managing stress, coping when things go wrong and avoiding relapse. Families have their own weekly virtual meeting with addiction counsellors, where they get information about addiction and a place to talk to other families going through the same thing.

pillars.title: Clear Rules and a Steady Routine
pillars.body: HOPE Be The Cure keeps a structured daily routine and firm rules. The client agreement sets a zero tolerance policy for alcohol and drugs on and off the property, and clients can be screened at any time. The first 10 days are a suitability period. Fees are charged monthly in advance, and leaving early needs 30 days written notice. If medical detox is needed, it has to happen elsewhere before admission. It is worth reading the agreement on the centre's website before you commit.

overviewH2: HOPE Be The Cure: Centre Overview
overview: HOPE Be The Cure treats alcohol, opioid, fentanyl, cocaine and methamphetamine addiction in a residential setting, and its recovery.com profile also lists benzodiazepines, heroin and ecstasy. Counselling is the core of the program: cognitive behavioural therapy, psychotherapy, psycho-educational workshops and a relapse prevention plan. The centre says its wider team includes psychotherapists, behavioural therapists and peer support workers alongside the addiction counsellors.

location.heading: HOPE Be The Cure in Innisfil, Ontario
location.intro: HOPE Be The Cure is in Innisfil, a lakeside town in Simcoe County that sits between Barrie and Bradford on the west shore of Lake Simcoe. Toronto is about an hour south on Highway 400, Barrie is 15 to 20 minutes away, and Bradford, Newmarket and Orillia are each roughly 25 to 45 minutes by car.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and its recovery.com profile. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What kind of program is HOPE Be The Cure?
faqs.a: HOPE Be The Cure is a private residential addiction program, so clients live at the house while they are in treatment. It has five beds and a staffing ratio the centre gives as 1 to 3. Former clients and families can also join weekly aftercare and family support groups.

faqs.q: Where is HOPE Be The Cure located?
faqs.a: The house is at 752 Pinegrove Avenue in Innisfil, Ontario, in Simcoe County on the south side of Barrie. Toronto is about an hour away by Highway 400, and Barrie is roughly 15 to 20 minutes by car. Call admissions before you travel so they can plan your arrival.

faqs.q: How much does HOPE Be The Cure cost?
faqs.a: The centre does not publish its prices, and its recovery.com profile says to call for rates. Its client agreement describes a monthly service fee paid in advance, which does not cover prescription medication or outside therapists. Ask admissions for the current fee on your first call.

faqs.q: How long does the program last?
faqs.a: HOPE Be The Cure does not publish a fixed program length. Fees are charged by the month, and the client agreement asks for 30 days written notice before leaving. Admissions can tell you how long most clients stay.

faqs.q: Does HOPE Be The Cure offer detox?
faqs.a: No medical detox is listed on site. The centre's recovery.com profile marks detox as not offered, and the client agreement says some people may need medical detox elsewhere before admission. If you are drinking heavily or using opioids, ask admissions how to arrange withdrawal management first.

Clients get two 60-minute one-to-one sessions a week with a certified addiction counsellor, plus daily group workshops. The centre also lists cognitive behavioural therapy, psychotherapy, relapse prevention, psycho-educational workshops and at least three 12-step meetings a week. Yoga, meditation, breathwork, reiki, fitness, gardening and cooking classes fill out the day.

faqs.q: What addictions does HOPE Be The Cure treat?
faqs.a: The centre runs programs for alcohol, opioid, fentanyl, cocaine and methamphetamine addiction. Its recovery.com profile adds benzodiazepines, heroin and ecstasy, along with co-occurring conditions such as anxiety, depression and PTSD.

Graduates can join a weekly in-person aftercare group that runs for 90 minutes and is led by a certified addictions counsellor. It covers stress, coping and relapse prevention, and it keeps you in touch with people who went through the program. Families can join a separate weekly virtual support group.

faqs.q: Is it private? Can I use my benefits?
faqs.a: Yes, HOPE Be The Cure is a private, fee-based program, and its recovery.com profile lists private pay as the payment option. No insurers are listed. If you have extended health benefits, ask admissions for receipts and check with your plan.

The program has a zero tolerance policy for alcohol and drugs, on or off the property, and clients can be asked for a drug or alcohol screen at any time. The first 10 days are treated as a suitability period. A credit card is kept on file at intake for medication and other small expenses.
